sentiment.rationale: The document shows significant improvement in key metrics: revenue up 35% to $22.7B, core loss per share narrowed from ($2.90) to ($1.24), and operating cash flow turned positive at $0.2B versus a large outflow last year. Management expresses confidence in the recovery plan, with progress on production rates and a positive free cash flow outlook for Q4. However, the company still reports a GAAP net loss, faces risks from tariffs and certification delays, and guidance is cautiously optimistic rather than strongly raised, preventing a higher score.

summary.revenue: $22.7 billion, up 35% from $16.9 billion in Q2 2024, primarily reflecting 150 commercial deliveries.
summary.eps: GAAP diluted loss per share of ($0.92) compared to ($2.33) in Q2 2024; core loss per share (non-GAAP) of ($1.24) compared to ($2.90) in Q2 2024.
summary.guidance: Third quarter free cash flow expected to be more or less in line with Q2 usage before any DOJ payment, setting up for positive free cash flow in Q4. Full-year free cash flow expected around ($3) billion. BCA margins expected to be negative for the year but improving quarter by quarter. 737 deliveries expected to be a little better than 400 for the full year; 787 deliveries at the high end of the 70-80 range.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of (0.8)% compared to (6.5)% in Q2 2024; core operating margin (non-GAAP) of (1.9)% compared to (8.3)% in Q2 2024.
key_risks: Potential $700 million one-time payment related to the DOJ non-prosecution agreement in Q3.
Certification delays for 737-7 and 737-10, now expected in 2026.
Dynamic global trade environment and potential tariff impacts, though some agreements are resolving.
Work stoppage risk from a strike involving about 3,200 employees in St. Louis and St. Charles.
Remaining work on fixed-price development programs in Defense, Space & Security.
key_opportunities: Strong market demand with total company backlog of $619 billion, including over 5,900 commercial airplanes.
Planned production rate increases for 737 (to 42 per month) and 787 (beyond 7 per month).
Recent large orders including 120 787 and 30 777-9 for Qatar Airways and 32 787-10 for British Airways.
Defense wins including a $2.8 billion contract from U.S. Space Force and increased national defense spending from the Reconciliation Bill.
Favorable trade deals (e.g., US-EU agreement) that could reduce tariff impacts.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management states 'our recovery plan is taking hold' and 'we're starting to see real momentum,' while acknowledging remaining work, reflecting a confident but measured tone.
